content:
maria-g: starting a thread to decide how we actually isolate per-customer telemetry exports. current ask: per-tenant OTLP exporters + retention/quotas. input?
kevin: 👍 high level sounds right. question: do we route at the collector (split by org_id) or in the exporter layer?
samir: prefer split at collector so downstream exporters are simple and we can apply retention policies before the sink. downside: collector configs explode.
liz-devex: UX concern — users will expect a single view in the console for their traces/metrics. how do we tie the exported dataset back to a tenant in the console?
ana-sre: (typo in name) apologize ignore
ana-sre: will the console query different indices per tenant, or a single index with tenant tag? cost + RBAC tradeoffs.
maria-g: good call. two patterns: 1) per-tenant namespace -> separate storage buckets/indices (strong isolation, easier billing), 2) shared index with tenant_id tag + strict RBAC (cheaper ops, harder to enforce legal separation).
kevin: from infra side, separate buckets means we can apply per-bucket lifecycle rules (retention) which matches requirements. but more overhead for onboarding and routing.
samir: routing sketch: collector receives spans with resource.attributes.org_id or auth token claims. collector uses processor to set export destination: e.g. export_map[org_id] -> s3://redwood-telemetry/tenants/<org>/traces/ or otlp endpoint. config snippet:```yaml
processors:
  tenant_router:
    mapping:
      from: resource.attributes.org_id
      to_path: "tenants/${value}"
exporters:
  aws_s3/tenantA:
    bucket: redwood-telemetry-tenantA
```
jeff-product: are we comfortable trusting resource.attributes.org_id? lots of SDKs attach org_id incorrectly. need to tie to auth.
kevin: agree — must validate against the token in the request. collector should reject mismatches. propose we accept X-ORG-ID header only if TLS client cert or mTLS paired to token. otherwise derive from token claim.
maria-g: +1. can we centralize validation in auth processor? token -> org claim -> canonical_org. then drop incoming org_id if mismatch and tag with canonical_org so routing is consistent.
ana-sre: (typo again) okay
ana-sre: RBAC: if we do per-bucket, we can give tenant admins access to their bucket via IAM role. If shared index, RBAC needs app-level filtering and strong encryption key scoping.
samir: cost gating idea: attach a telemetry quota recorder that increments per-tenant token/ingest rate and can return a 429 from the collector when over budget. implementation: processor checks counters in redis and sets status. cheap and visible.
kevin: small worry: 429s from collector will surface to app teams as random errors. need a clear error message and Console chart showing quota usage + last 429 time.
liz-devex: I'll add a quota/card in the console — color banding and notifications + webhook for infra teams. also need a rollout plan for this feature flag.
maria-g: rollout: start with opt-in tenants on dedicated exporters, monitor latency + cost for 2 weeks, then auto-enroll high-volume tenants if they opt in. use canary with header X-TELEMETRY-ROUTE=per-tenant for a subset.
jeff-product: product note: some enterprise customers will request air-gapped exports -> per-tenant on-prem exporter config. make sure our design supports mapping org -> custom exporter URL.
samir: operational TODOs: 1) auth processor that canonicalizes org from token 2) tenant router processor 3) quota processor with metrics 4) exporters templating + onboarding docs.
kevin: security TODO: threat model for spoofed org_id in payloads, ensure auth processor cannot be bypassed.
liz-devex: I'll draft console UX flows and onboarding checklist. want a quick mock by EOD Friday.
maria-g: timeline proposal: alpha in 3 weeks for opt-in tenants, beta with quota enforcement in 8 weeks. objections?
ana-sre: (typo) done
ana-sre: no objections, want SLO runbook for failures where collector rejects telemetry.
kevin: agree, add a fallback policy: if per-tenant exporter is unreachable, fall back to shared-export (with tag) and emit audit event. configurable per-tenant.
samir: note: fallback increases blast radius for data separation; need explicit opt-in fallback flag.
maria-g: agreed. I'll capture decisions and open RFC PR. tagging @ops-bot to create a tracking ticket. :spiral_notepad:
ops-bot: Created ticket INFRA-7892: "Per-tenant telemetry routing + quotas" assigned to eng-platform, due 2026-04-12.
kevin: thanks — will start auth processor prototype today.
liz-devex: will set up console card story in Jira and link to INFRA-7892.
maria-g: thanks everyone. I'll drop the RFC link once PR is up.
